skill.name: executor-architecture
skill.description: Document system architecture, decisions, interface contracts, and component designs after choosing an approach and before writing specifications.
skill.summary: Create linked architecture documents with explicit boundaries, decision criteria, interface lifecycles, and human approval gates.
skill.author: atri10

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are Markdown formatting, fixed sibling paths, or document identifiers rather than executable backticks, path traversal exploits, or reconnaissance. Required helper executions remain confirmed with low confidence because their implementations are outside the five reviewed files. Verification can record a passed phase before human approval; no evidence found of exfiltration, credential theft, or audit-directed prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Required helper implementations are outside the reviewed skill package.
remediation.suggestion: Declare and pin the helper dependency, include its implementations in the audit scope, and verify trusted repository paths before execution.

remediation.issue: Verification instructs recording architecture approval before the human gate.
remediation.suggestion: Use read-only validation before the gate. Record a passed phase only after explicit human approval, and require approval evidence for that transition.

content.value_statement: Vague architecture leaves teams with incompatible interfaces and undocumented decisions. This skill structures architecture, decisions, contracts, and component designs for human review before specification.
actual_capabilities: Draft architecture documents covering constraints, components, dependency boundaries, data flow, failure modes, and deployment.
Record decisions with viable alternatives, accepted costs, observable reversal criteria, and reversibility labels.
Specify interface signatures, types, errors, lifecycle rules, stability states, and named consumers.
Describe component state, algorithms, edge cases, test dependencies, and file responsibilities.
Maintain document links, initiative indexes, explicit skips, and supersession history.
Prepare architecture and design review summaries with human approval gates.
limitations: Requires the sibling executor skill, its references, and helper scripts, which are not included in this package.
Requires an existing initiative charter and an accepted approach or explicitly skipped discovery.
Produces documentation and interface contract text, not implementation code or executed application tests.
Helper safety is unverified, and the verification checklist conflicts with the stated approval sequence.

use_cases.title: Define System Boundaries
use_cases.description: Turn an accepted approach into component responsibilities, dependency rules, failure responses, and reviewable architecture.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Shared Interfaces
use_cases.description: Define exact operations, types, errors, and ordering so independently assigned tasks can integrate against the same contract.

use_cases.title: Preserve Decision History
use_cases.description: Record alternatives and reversal criteria, then supersede outdated decisions without deleting their original reasoning.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Architecture Overview
prompt_templates.prompt: For [initiative], use the charter and accepted approach to draft the architecture overview. State constraints, component responsibilities, boundaries, and open questions. Stop for human review before recording approval.

prompt_templates.title: Record an Architecture Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: For [initiative], document the decision about [topic]. Compare viable alternatives, accepted costs, reversibility, and observable reversal criteria. Link the decision to the architecture and prepare it for review.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Shared Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: For [initiative], define the interface between [provider] and [consumer]. Specify exact operations, types, errors, ordering, concurrency, lifecycle, stability, and consumers. Identify missing information without inventing implementation details.

prompt_templates.title: Supersede a Frozen Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: For [initiative], evaluate replacing [frozen interface] because [new evidence]. Draft its successor, affected consumer updates, decision rationale, and component design changes. Preserve prior document bodies and request approval before recording phase completion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage an architectural change during execution

output_examples.input: Document architecture for tenant placement using the accepted per-cell storage approach.
output: Components: placement policy, storage port, storage adapter, and HTTP adapter.
Boundary: policy depends only on policy-owned interfaces; the storage adapter implements the storage port.
Decision record: compare per-cell storage with shared storage and state the accepted operational costs.
Review: confirm failure responses and interface contracts before recording architecture approval.

output_examples.input: Two tasks disagree about the placement interface. Define the contract before implementation.
output: Operations: list candidate cells, bind a tenant, and release a tenant.
Types: define identifier formats, capacity units, and timestamp precision.
Errors: specify unavailable storage, existing placement, and a cell that stopped accepting requests.
Lifecycle: require initialization, document concurrent calls, and name both consuming tasks.

output_examples.input: A storage decision no longer satisfies measured requirements. Replace it without losing history.
output: New decision record: describe the changed constraint and the evidence that triggered reconsideration.
Alternatives: compare viable replacements and state migration costs.
History: link the successor and predecessor while preserving the original decision body.
Dependencies: update affected architecture references and initiative index entries.

best_practices: Provide the initiative charter, accepted approach, and measured constraints before drafting architecture.
Review helper implementations and dependency paths before execution; keep validation read-only until explicit human approval.
Keep contracts exact, index documents in the same change, and preserve superseded reasoning.
anti_patterns: Starting specifications or recording passed phases before human approval.
Letting separate tasks invent shared signatures, error contracts, or ordering rules.
Editing historical decision bodies or frozen interfaces instead of writing linked successor documents.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It guides architecture documents, decision records, interface contracts, and component designs. Outputs include linked metadata, review summaries, and explicit skip records.

faq.question: Does it write implementation code?
faq.answer: No. It permits signatures and type declarations as interface contract text, but implementation belongs to later phases.

faq.question: Can it run independently?
faq.answer: The full workflow requires the sibling executor skill, shared references, helper scripts, and an existing initiative inside a Git repository.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The package contains Markdown instructions and templates rather than tool-specific executable integrations.

faq.question: When can documents be skipped?
faq.answer: Skip decisions without viable alternatives, designs with obvious internals, or interfaces without shared boundaries. Record reasons explicitly; skipping architecture requires human waiver.

faq.question: What security precautions are needed?
faq.answer: Review required helper scripts before running them. Keep credentials out of documents, and record passed phases only after explicit human approval.
